title: TSG vs RMP
summary: Starve them, then swap. The Mage holds four answers and two of them are escapes, not mitigation — he dies when they are gone, not before.

sections.title: The opening is when they are dry, not when you are ready
sections.body: Counts: Rogue 6, Priest 5, Mage 4. The Mage is thinnest and two of his four — Ice Block and Greater Invisibility — are escapes that reset the go rather than surviving it. So the first two goes are strips, not kills. You are looking for the moment nobody on their side holds a trinket, and then you CC to end it rather than to start it.

sections.title: Strip — force the cheap answers out

steps.note: On the Mage. He blinks the moment he is free, so lead with it.
On the Priest. Denies Pain Suppression, not the heal.
45s. Up nearly every go — this is the sustained term.

sections.title: The kill go — once their trinkets are down

steps.note: On the Priest. Free, and their answer to it is a trinket.
90s. Only spend it into a pool you have already emptied.
90s. Aligns with Avatar — keep them on one clock.
Fresh stun DR after Storm Bolt. The window, not the opener.
120s immunity. Resets your go entirely — do not burst into it.
120s. He leaves; he does not survive.
30s. Back every go, so it is not worth forcing.

sections.title: Which side the clock favours
sections.body: Yours. You hold 20 answers to their 15 and the Druid has no damage cooldowns to waste. A failed go costs you very little, which is the whole reason the strip-first plan is correct here and would be wrong in the mirror.
